task.description: Decide the appropriate disposition for a graduate student's proposed thesis defense by integrating distributed evidence about manuscript readiness, academic milestones, committee assessments, examiner arrangements, outstanding requirements, and feasible next steps, and record one disposition with a justification.

timeline.author: organization_system
timeline.content: Participants are coordinating the assigned organizational task.

timeline.author: Felix Alvarez
timeline.content:
- The student told me that their most recent journal submission was returned for major revisions, but after comparing the current thesis draft against my previous comments I found that only localized changes remain and no substantial new research cycle is needed before defense, even though the journal decision has made the student doubt whether the thesis is ready.
- I will be away on a six-week research visit later this term, and scheduling Mei Johansson's defense before I leave would avoid pushing it into the following term.
- Felix Alvarez is dealing with a prolonged probate process after a relative's death.
- Felix Alvarez has filed a workplace grievance about a former manager.

timeline.author: Noah Kowalski
timeline.content:
- After reviewing the student's progress, the committee endorses moving forward to defense as the work now stands.
- A senior researcher in Mei Johansson's area will be visiting campus in two weeks and has asked to attend the defense, so that would be an unusually attractive time to schedule Mei Johansson.
- Noah Kowalski still owes money from a small business that closed last year.
- Noah Kowalski is on a debt-repayment plan after several months of missed bills.

timeline.author: Liam Adeyemi
timeline.content:
- Our group normally asks students to complete a full mock defense before the formal defense, and Mei Johansson has not yet done one, so I would treat the case as ready only on that condition.
- At a recent practice research talk, Mei Johansson became visibly nervous and struggled with several audience questions, which makes me think they need more time before a defense.
- Liam Adeyemi owes a close friend money and is embarrassed about the delay in repaying it.
- Liam Adeyemi recently ended an engagement and is finding it hard.

timeline.author: Carlos Okonkwo
timeline.content:
- The administrative review of the defense package is done: all required documents are received, and the only item returned is a margin and heading formatting correction to make before final submission, which does not hold up authorization to schedule.
- Carlos Okonkwo's partner recently lost their job and the household is relying on one income.
- Carlos Okonkwo has been helping a close family member through a rehabilitation programme.

timeline.author: Nadia Gupta
timeline.content:
- The student explained that an ongoing family situation has disrupted their ability to deal with university paperwork and asked that correspondence not be sent to their home; the academic record nevertheless shows that one required pre-defense milestone remains incomplete.
- Nadia Gupta has not spoken to a sibling since a family argument last year.
- Nadia Gupta is waiting for a decision on a visa renewal application.

timeline.author: Andrei Hassan
timeline.content:
- A colleague told me that the examiner often leaves appointment paperwork until the last minute, but the examiner has passed the eligibility check and has indicated willingness to act, with only the formal appointment confirmation still outstanding, which the colleague said is typical of how they handle administrative forms.
- Andrei Hassan is contesting an inheritance with a sibling.
- Andrei Hassan is temporarily staying with a friend while looking for a new place to live.

timeline.author: Tariq Mensah
timeline.content: - Tariq Mensah is in a dispute with their landlord over repairs to the apartment.

timeline.author: Mei Johansson
timeline.content: - Mei Johansson is in a dispute with their landlord over repairs to the apartment.

timeline.author: task_system
timeline.content:
GRADUATE PROGRAM — DEFENSE READINESS DECISION REQUIRED
Source: Graduate Program Office · To: Sanjay Ibrahim
Review the available task-relevant information for the proposed thesis defense and record exactly one disposition: ready_to_schedule, ready_with_conditions, defer_pending_requirements, or not_ready_reassess_later. Include explanation of the evidence supporting the selected disposition.

description: Decide the appropriate disposition for a graduate student's proposed thesis defense by integrating distributed evidence about manuscript readiness, academic milestones, committee assessments, examiner arrangements, outstanding requirements, and feasible next steps, and record one disposition with a justification.
